mappings.note: Title matches: 'Cantique. Psaume d'Asaph.' vs 'En sang. En salme av Asaf.'
Content matches: Plea for God not to be silent.
Content matches: Enemies agitating and lifting heads.
Content matches: Plots against God's people.
Content matches: 'Let us wipe them out... so Israel's name is not remembered'.
Content matches: Conspiring with one heart/alliance against God.
Content matches: List of nations (Edom, Ishmaelites, Moab, Hagarenes).
Content matches: List of nations (Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, Philistines, Tyre).
Content matches: Assyria joining them. Note: 'Sela' in OSMAIN corresponds to '(Sélah.)' in translation.
Content matches: Comparison to Midian, Sisera, Jabin at Kishon.
Content matches: Destruction at En-Dor and becoming dung for the earth.
Content matches: Comparison of leaders to Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah, and Salmunna.
Content matches: 'Let us take God's pastures'.
Content matches: Make them like whirling thistledown/chaff.
Content matches: Fire consuming forest and mountains.
Content matches: Pursue with storm and fill with terror.
Content matches: Fill face with shame so they seek God's name.
Content matches: Let them be ashamed, terrified, confounded, and perish.

This verse exists in the translation but has no corresponding text in the provided OSMAIN text (which ends at v18). This is a known difference where some translations include a doxology or concluding statement not present in the specific Norwegian master text version provided here.

extraContent.description: The translation includes verse 19: 'Et qu'ils connaissent que toi seul, qui t'appelles l'Éternel, tu es le souverain de toute la terre.' (And let them know that you alone, whose name is the Lord, are the Most High over all the earth). This text is completely absent from the provided OSMAIN text.
